home.title: Any video, in Arabic, right on time.

library.title: Library

batch.title: A whole playlist or channel
batch.lead: Paste the link and let it work through the videos one by one. You can leave it running overnight.

settings.title: Settings

settings.defaultsLead: Used when you open a new video and when making files.
settings.voiceHint: Automatic picks a voice that matches the speaker in MP4s
settings.shortcutsLead: They work on the watch page, with Arabic keyboard layouts too.
settings.watchingLead: How the video page looks: the transcript beside the video, the timeline under it, the light around it. Also changed from the transcript's display button.

watch.followHint: It moves with the sentence being said. When you read elsewhere, a button brings you back.

watch.timelineHint: Shows where people speak and what is translated, and the sentence when you hover over it.

ai.lead: Plain machine translation can come out formal and long. With this on, an AI model writes the dub script in natural speech, fitted to the time of each sentence, and enables summaries and questions.

key.helpOther: Kept on this computer only and never shown again. Ollama needs no key.

model.helpClaude: Default {model}. A two-hour video costs roughly two or three dollars, and every sentence is cached so you never pay twice.

localOnly.title: Open this page on the computer itself
localOnly.body: AI settings hold a secret key, so they can only be changed from the computer Tarjuman runs on, not from a phone or another device on the network.

phone.lead: Open Tarjuman on your phone over the same Wi-Fi. Each device is paired once, and an unpaired device can't reach your files.
phone.qrLabel: QR code to pair a phone
phone.step1: Connect the phone to the same Wi-Fi.
phone.step2: Point the camera at the code and open the link.
phone.step3: Tarjuman opens on the phone and stays paired.
phone.firewall: On Windows, if the phone can't open the link, run scripts/allow-phone.ps1 once as administrator.
phone.resetDone: All devices were unpaired. Here is a new code.
phone.remote: This device is paired. Pairing is managed from the computer running Tarjuman.
phone.noLan: This computer isn't on a local network right now, so a phone can't be paired.
phone.unpairedTitle: This device isn't paired with Tarjuman
phone.unpairedBody: To protect your files, Tarjuman opens on other devices only after they are paired once.
phone.unpaired1: On the computer, open Tarjuman, then Settings, then Phone.
phone.unpaired2: Scan the QR code with this device's camera, or open the link under it.
phone.codeDone: A new code was made. Paired devices stay paired.
phone.codeHint: One code pairs any number of phones. A new code stops the old one without unpairing anyone.
phone.noDevices: No phone is paired yet. Scan the code with your phone and it will show up here.
phone.codeLife: Minutes left for this code: {n}. Then a new one appears by itself.

extensions.lead: Browser extensions allowed to use Tarjuman. The first one that connects is trusted automatically; any other waits for your approval here.
extensions.getItHint: Its page opens in the Chrome Web Store, where you add it.

storage.lead: What Tarjuman keeps on this computer. Clearing a cache is safe: it is rebuilt when needed, and your translation corrections are never cleared.
storage.voicesHint: The least recently used are removed automatically above {limit}
storage.tmpHint: Left by interrupted jobs; cleared at every start

privacy.lead: Your files stay on your computer. Some features send text or a request to an online service to work. This is the full list: what leaves, who receives it, and the alternative that sends nothing.
privacy.never: No accounts, no usage statistics, no tracking. Video and audio are never uploaded to any service.

captions.name: YouTube captions
captions.what: The video link is sent to YouTube to fetch the captions that come with it.
captions.local: Alternative: upload a video file from your computer; its speech is transcribed locally.

translate.name: Translation
translate.what: The video's sentences are sent as text to Google Translate, and to MyMemory when Google is unavailable. The result is saved here, so a sentence is not sent twice.
translate.local: There is no local alternative for translation yet. Without internet only saved sentences work.

voice.name: Dub voice
voice.what: The text of each translated sentence and the chosen voice name are sent to Microsoft's Edge voice service, and to Google when nothing else works. The clip is saved here.
voice.local: Alternative: the local Arabic voice, Piper, works without internet and is used by itself when the service fails.

fetch.name: Video download
fetch.what: When you make an MP4 or download a video from a site, the video is requested from that site.
fetch.local: Alternative: a file already on your computer.

ai.name: AI (optional)
ai.what: Off until you turn it on. When on, the video's text, and your question if you ask one, are sent to the provider you chose.
ai.local: Alternative: leave it off, or choose a server that runs on your computer, such as Ollama.

models.name: Model downloads
models.what: The Whisper, local voice and music separation models are downloaded once from Hugging Face and GitHub. None of your data goes with the request.
models.local: After the first download they work without internet.

whisper.name: Speech recognition (Whisper)
whisper.what: Speech is turned into text on your computer. The audio never leaves it.

separate.name: Separating the speaker from the music
separate.what: Runs on your computer with a local model.

files.name: Your files and settings
files.what: Videos, subtitles, saved words, settings and the AI key stay in the data folder on your computer.

updates.name: Update checks
updates.what: Every few hours Tarjuman asks GitHub for the list of newer versions, and downloads the installer when you choose to update. Nothing about you or your videos is sent.
updates.local: Alternative: turn off "Check for updates automatically" in Settings → Updates.

desktop.lead: What happens when you minimize or close the Tarjuman window, and whether it starts with Windows. Each choice is independent.
desktop.windowsOnly: These settings are for the Windows app.
desktop.notApp: These settings are saved now, but they work only when Tarjuman runs as the desktop app: from the installed shortcut, or with this command:
desktop.minimizeToTrayHint: The window is hidden when you minimize it, and the Tarjuman icon stays next to the clock.
desktop.closeToTrayHint: Tarjuman stays in the notification area when you close the window. To exit, choose Quit Tarjuman from the icon's menu.
desktop.startWithWindowsHint: Tarjuman starts in the notification area when you sign in, without opening a window.
desktop.keepEngine: Keep the engine running after the window closes
desktop.keepEngineHint: Translation and dubbing stay available to the browser extension, and running jobs finish. The Tarjuman icon stays so you can quit it.
desktop.extensionNeedsEngine: The browser extension's features need the engine running. When it is stopped, the extension shows "Not connected".

updates.lead: Tarjuman looks for a newer version on its GitHub releases page, and shows you what was added and fixed before you update.
updates.checkFailed: Couldn't reach GitHub. Check the internet connection and try again.
updates.installHint: The installer is downloaded and its checksum verified; then Tarjuman closes, updates and starts again. Windows will ask for permission.
updates.jobsRunning: Jobs are running, and updating stops them.
updates.fromSource: You run Tarjuman from source: update it with git pull, then restart it.
updates.noChecksum: This version has no checksum file, so download its installer from its page.
updates.checkAutoHint: Every few hours, asks GitHub for newer versions. Nothing about you or your videos is sent.
updates.autoHint: When a newer version is found and no job is running, it is installed without asking (Windows still asks for permission). Installed app only.
updates.installHintLinux: The new AppImage is downloaded, its checksum verified, and it replaces this one. Restart Tarjuman afterwards.
updates.restart: Version {v} is downloaded and has replaced the old one. Close Tarjuman and open it again to use it.

record.hint: Speak, or let it hear a lecture, then stop: the recording is saved on this computer, transcribed and translated by itself.
record.denied: The microphone isn't allowed. Allow it from the lock icon next to the address, then try again.
record.deniedApp: The microphone was refused in the Tarjuman window. Click the button to give it back: the window closes and opens again with it allowed.

asrSet.lead: Whisper turns speech into text on your computer. Accuracy depends above all on the model size, and bigger models need a stronger computer, so this shows your computer, the model that suits it, and why.
asrSet.gpuNoCuda: Present, but the CUDA 12 libraries aren't installed, so it can't be used yet.
asrSet.speed: about {n} s per minute of audio
asrSet.notInstalled: Whisper isn't installed. Run: python -m tarjuman setup
asrSet.onDisk: {model} is downloaded and loads on the first transcription.
asrSet.notYet: {model} isn't downloaded yet ({size}). It downloads on the first transcription, or now with this button.
asrSet.languageHint: Automatic detects it from the start of the file. If your recordings are always Arabic, choose Arabic: the language is never misdetected and speech is never translated instead of written down.
asrSet.styleHint: Whisper is given a sentence in this style before the audio and follows it: spelling, punctuation, and dialect words as spoken. Used only with Arabic speech.
asrSet.qualityHint: More accurate weighs five candidates per sentence and keeps the best (a little slower). Faster takes the first.
asrSet.enhanceHint: Removes hum and hiss and evens out the volume. Helps noisy or quiet recordings; may not help clean ones.
asrSet.vadHint: Stops Whisper from inventing sentences in long silences. Leave it on unless quiet words go missing.
asrSet.deviceHint: A graphics card is much faster than the CPU.
asrSet.honest: No automatic transcription is 100% accurate: clarity, noise, overlapping voices and dialect all matter. These settings get as close as possible: the bigger model matters most, then setting the language, then the writing style. You can correct any sentence by hand in the transcript, or transcribe the file again after changing the settings.
asrSet.gpuOld: An old card: it doesn't speed these models up, so transcription runs on the CPU. Nothing to install.
asrSet.deleted: The {model} model was deleted, {size} freed. It downloads again if used later.
asrSet.vocabHint: On the right, write a word the way it should appear (a name, a product, an English word): Whisper is told it before transcribing. If Whisper keeps writing it wrong in a certain way, put that on the left and it is replaced after transcribing. Works best with large-v3.
asrSet.aiFixHint: After Whisper, the AI reads the whole transcript and fixes misheard words from the context, without changing the dialect or rewording anything. The text (not the audio) is sent to the AI provider you chose.
asrSet.termsSaved: Words saved. They are used on the next transcription, or click “Transcribe again” on an older recording.
asrSet.otherLead: Any Whisper model in faster-whisper's format (CTranslate2): its name on Hugging Face as on its page, or the path of its folder on this computer. It is checked before anything is downloaded.
asrSet.otherOnDisk: On this computer, nothing to download
asrSet.otherWarn: A third-party model: its accuracy is its author's. Try it on a recording you know the words of, and compare.
asrSet.otherAdded: {model} added and chosen. It is used on the next transcription.
asrSet.speedGuess: about {n} s per minute of audio (estimate)
asrSet.removed: {model} was taken off the list. Its folder is still on this computer.

useHint.audio: Usually short, so accuracy matters most.
useHint.video: From this computer, YouTube or any site. Usually long, so accuracy and speed balanced.
useHint.live: Must keep up with the video, so speed matters most.

asrSet.useNow: Using now: {model} · about {n} s per minute
asrSet.twoInMemory: Two models stay in memory, so moving between a recording, a video and live captions needs no reload.
asrSet.oneInMemory: This computer's memory holds one model at a time: switching between two reloads it.
